newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee slips on foreign strength of dlr.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee slips on foreign strength of dlr.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee opened weaker against the dollar on Friday due to overseas gains by the greenback, dealers said.
At 0530 GMT the rupee was at 58.50 to the dollar, after opening at 58.45. The rupee closed at 58.40 on Thursday.
"The rupee opened low since banks had factored in overseas gains by the dollar," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the greenback by five local cents in line with its overseas gains, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.3754 and 59.5547, dealers said.
Dealers are mixed on whether the exchange rate would remain volatile.
"I think the exchange rate will stay at current levels due to import covering on one side and selling on the other," said the HongKong bank dealer.
"I feel there is huge upside potential since the Central Bank's top level is almost one rupee away," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were at 12 percent, after opening at 11.5 and rising to 13.5, dealers said.
